brief.headline: Korean memory massacre: 2x levered ETF mechanics trigger 9%+ wipeout ahead of $646bn capex reveal Monday
brief.summary: <cite index="45-2,45-4">Samsung Electronics fell 12.31% and SK Hynix fell 12.47% in their worst 1-day showing since the 2008 financial crisis</cite>, driven by structural dislocations from <cite index="45-8,45-10">single-stock leverage and inverse ETFs launched May 27 that pulled in $9 billion by June 23</cite>. <cite index="37-2,37-3">Samsung and SK Hynix are preparing to announce hundreds of billions of dollars worth in new investments Monday, with Samsung Group unveiling a 1,000 trillion won ($646 billion) spending package over the next decade</cite>. <cite index="10-2,10-7">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 90-95% QoQ in Q1 2026, with Q2 forecast at 58-63% QoQ; NAND Flash contract prices jumped 70-75% QoQ in Q2</cite>. <cite index="19-2,19-6">The five largest US hyperscalers collectively committed $660-690 billion on capex in 2026, nearly doubling 2025 levels, with all reporting supply-constrained markets</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="5-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% of global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025, followed by Samsung at 22% and Micron at 21%</cite>. <cite index="4-16">SK Hynix is the only supplier able to deliver both HBM3E and next-generation HBM4 at scale</cite>, with <cite index="9-8">HBM4 expected to command prices roughly 40% higher than HBM3E even after absorbing a 50% rise in cost per bit</cite>. Samsung continues to trail in HBM qualification and time-to-market. Long SK Hynix vs Samsung remains the cleanest expression of HBM mix shift and pricing power through 2027, though Friday's levered-ETF-induced dislocation compressed the valuation gap artificially. Watch Monday's capex announcement for Samsung's HBM4 timeline and foundry diversification plans that could narrow the gap structurally.

memory_cycle.stage: Mid-upcycle plateau with AI-driven structural reallocation
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="14-1,14-8">DRAM and NAND are in a structural reallocation to HBM, not a cyclical shortage, holding prices elevated through 2027 and likely resetting the long-term floor</cite>. <cite index="11-11,11-12">TrendForce projects global memory market at $551.6bn in 2026, rising to $842.7bn in 2027; DRAM revenue up 144% YoY hitting $404.3bn</cite>. <cite index="14-18">IDC expects 2026 DRAM supply growth of only 16% YoY, with NAND at 17% YoY, both below 20-30% historical norms</cite>. <cite index="17-3,17-7">Q1 2026 conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93-98% QoQ; Q2 DRAM decelerated but NAND is now rising faster than DRAM for the first time this cycle</cite>. Spot momentum fading but contract pricing remains structurally supported through at least Q4 2026.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="4-4,4-20">Top three memory makers have already allocated their full HBM output for the year, with Micron guiding for a 68% gross margin in Q2 2026</cite>. <cite index="4-12">HBM3E consumes roughly three times the wafer area of standard DDR5 due to larger dies and yield losses from vertical stacking</cite>. <cite index="9-6">HBM bit shipments are projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1 billion gigabits</cite>, with <cite index="9-7">SK Hynix expecting only a minimal to modest downtick in HBM3E pricing for 2026 vs 2025</cite>. SK Hynix dominant in HBM4 early ramp, Samsung still fighting for Nvidia qualification. Supply remains fully committed through 2026.

key_filings.summary_en: Presidential briefing at Blue House Monday June 29 to unveil Samsung's 1,000 trillion won ($646bn) decade-long semiconductor spending plan and SK Hynix joint investment announcements as part of 'National Briefing on Three Major Mega-Projects for the Great Leap Forward'

news_pulse.headline: Samsung & SK Hynix crash 9-12% Friday despite $646bn capex reveal Monday; 2x levered ETFs drove worst 1-day drop since 2008
news_pulse.implication: Market structure dislocation, not fundamental deterioration. Korean single-stock levered ETFs ($9bn AUM) created amplification loop into close. Capex announcement Monday could reverse technically but validates HBM capacity urgency.

news_pulse.headline: Q2 2026 DRAM contracts +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75% QoQ; NAND acceleration outpaces DRAM for first time
news_pulse.implication: Enterprise SSD demand from AI deployments now primary NAND driver. Consumer memory deprioritized. Validates Samsung/SK mix shift to high-margin AI infrastructure over commodity client segments.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex revised to $660-690bn (Microsoft/Alphabet/Amazon/Meta/Oracle), up 81% YoY, 207% vs 2024
news_pulse.implication: All hyperscalers report supply-constrained, not demand-constrained. Meta raised 2026 capex to $125-145bn citing higher component pricing (HBM/DRAM). Direct read-through to memory ASP sustainability.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS capacity to hit 130k wafers/month by end-2026, doubling 2024; Nvidia secured 60% of total capacity
news_pulse.implication: CoWoS remains primary bottleneck for HBM-enabled AI accelerators. Nvidia lock on majority capacity extends through 2026. AMD/Google fighting for remainder. Packaging, not HBM fab, gates incremental GPU shipments.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix 57% HBM revenue share Q4 2025, Samsung 22%, Micron 21%; only SK can deliver HBM3E+HBM4 at scale
news_pulse.implication: SK Hynix structural lead in next-gen HBM widens vs Samsung. Samsung still fighting Nvidia HBM3E qual. Monday capex announcement critical for Samsung HBM4 credibility and 2027 share trajectory.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM spot prices +3.57% weekly to $34.80 (DDR4 1Gx8-3200) but buyers hesitant to chase; NAND spot trading quiet
news_pulse.implication: First signs of spot exhaustion mid-Q2 2026. Contract pricing still climbing but parabolic phase maturing. Not a peak signal, more plateau forming. Validates TrendForce deceleration forecast for H2.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung P5 fab (Pyeongtaek) operational 2028, SK Hynix M15X fab mid-2027; 900k DRAM wafers/month committed to OpenAI Stargate
news_pulse.implication: New capacity 18-24 months out. 2026-2027 supply fully committed. Monday capex likely accelerates timelines but meaningful relief pushed to 2028. Tight supply thesis intact through next 6 quarters.

news_pulse.headline: Memory now 35% of PC build materials, up from 20% a year ago; DRAM lead times stretched beyond 40 weeks
news_pulse.implication: Structural cost inflation hitting downstream OEMs. Dell raised hardware prices 17% March 30. PC/smartphone demand destruction risk rising but hyperscaler willingness-to-pay overwhelms consumer weakness.

brief.derivatives_signal: KOSPI 200 futures triggered 5% Sidecar circuit breaker June 26; 2x levered single-stock ETFs created death-spiral into close with 6-7% NAV dislocations. OTC ADRs (SSNLF/HXSCL) likely gap higher Monday if capex details land cleanly. Options skew will price Monday binary. Avoid chasing Friday's technical dislocation; wait for post-announcement stabilization.
watch_for_next_3h: Korean market open Sunday evening ET: Samsung/SK Hynix price action post-Friday levered ETF flush—technical rebound likely but watch for institutional distribution
Samsung $646bn capex announcement Monday June 29: HBM4 timeline, fab locations, Nvidia design-win progress, foundry diversification strategy vs TSMC
SK Hynix capex details Monday: M15X fab acceleration, HBM4 volume ramp cadence, 2027 capacity allocation between Nvidia/AMD/hyperscalers
US semi sector reaction to Korean announcements: Micron/WDC relative performance, Applied Materials/Lam Research capex read-through, any hyperscaler commentary on memory procurement
TrendForce/DRAMeXchange June contract pricing updates: Q2 finalized ASPs, Q3 early guidance, any signs of spot-to-contract convergence signaling cycle maturation
